newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels rampage on leading Colombian highway.
newsitem.headline: Rebels rampage on leading Colombian highway.

text.p: Leftist rebels killed one person and torched 10 buses and a tractor-trailer truck on the main highway linking Colombia's capital to the northwest industrial hub of Medellin, authorities said on Wedneday.
Military spokesmen said the attacks occurred on Tuesday night along a winding stretch of the highway near the mountain town of San Luis, about 70 miles (115 km) east of Medellin.

A Bogota-based merchant identified as Francisco Javier Girlado, 36, was shot and killed when he tried to drive past a rebel roadblock and at least one other person was injured, police and military officials said.

Because of the attacks, in which at least 11 vehicles were gutted by flames, transportation companies suspended all cargo shipments along the highway, police said. The raids were carried out by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels who have ordered the suspension of all economic activity in the eastern part of Antioquia province this week, military officials said.

Medellin, Colombia's third largest city, is the capital of Antioquia, a province torn by frequent attacks by ELN and Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia rebels. The ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla group, was founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966 and specialises in a nationwide campaign of economic sabotage.
